title: extract-method and create-enum-helper through the compile gate by default
summary: extract-method / create-enum-helper --apply build the project before and after the write; no project found = REFUSED, --no-compile-gate writes unbuilt
intro: Read this when extract-method or create-enum-helper refuses with REFUSED (no-project) or (dirty-baseline), or when you want to know which project they build. Since 1.52 --apply goes through the compile gate without --project: the project is --project, else the project a DB at `<dir>\_D-RAG\<base>.sqlite` belongs to, else the nearest .dproj (walking up from the unit's folder) whose .dproj / .dpr names the unit. A project that does not build is refused; a fix that breaks the build is rolled back. No project = refused (exit 2).

questions.ask: Why did extract-method refuse with REFUSED (no-project)?
How do I extract a method without building the project?
Which project does create-enum-helper build before it writes?
